what: highlight "selling $75.5 billion worth of stock in the second quarter of 2024"
said: In just three months, his company, Berkshire Hathaway, sold about seventy-five billion dollars of Apple shares.

what: highlight "increasing its cash reserves to a record $276.9 billion"
said: That pushed its pile of cash to a record two hundred seventy-seven billion dollars. More cash than almost any company on Earth.

what: highlight "Originally a textile manufacturer, the company transitioned into a conglomerate starting in 1965"
said: Warren Buffett ran Berkshire Hathaway from nineteen seventy until twenty twenty-five. He turned an old textile company into one of the biggest companies in America.

what: highlight "reaching $700,000 in August 2024"
said: His company is so valuable that one of its top-class shares sold for seven hundred thousand dollars in twenty twenty-four. One share.

what: highlight "the biggest investment mistake he had ever made"
said: Funny enough, Buffett calls buying that old textile company his biggest investment mistake. He says it cost him about two hundred billion dollars in growth over forty-five years.

what: highlight "he wrote for an opinion piece published in the New York Times in 2008"
said: It said, Buy American. I am.

what: highlight "On September 23, 2008, Berkshire Hathaway acquired 10 percent of perpetual preferred stock of Goldman Sachs"
said: In September twenty oh eight, while Wall Street was in panic, Berkshire put money into Goldman Sachs, on very good terms.

what: highlight "the media reported that Buffett had agreed to buy General Electric (GE) preferred stock"
said: A month later, the news reported he was buying into General Electric too. He was shopping during the fire sale.

what: highlight "he had allocated capital too early resulting in suboptimal deals"
said: But here is the part people forget. Buffett did not time it perfectly. Critics said he moved too early, and some of his deals lost a lot of value at first.

what: highlight "suffered a 77% drop in earnings during Q3 2008"
said: His company's earnings fell seventy-seven percent in one quarter of two thousand eight. Even the greatest investor alive felt the crash.

what: highlight "In 2008, Buffett became the richest person in the world"
said: Buffett had become the richest person in the world in two thousand eight. Within a year, Forbes said he had lost about twenty-five billion dollars on paper.

what: highlight "where he became an expert dealing in the unregulated stock market of the day"
said: In the nineteen twenties, he made a fortune trading stocks on Wall Street, at a time when the market had almost no rules.

what: highlight "Kennedy later claimed he understood that the rampant stock speculation of the late 1920s would lead to a market crash ."
said: Kennedy later said he understood that all the wild speculation would end in a crash. So he got out.

what: highlight "but no evidence has been found of the anecdote"
said: It is a great story. But there is no evidence it ever happened. The earliest version of that tale was told about a different investor, decades later.

what: highlight "a complete lack of sentiment and a marvelous sense of timing"
said: One writer described why Kennedy survived. He had a passion for facts, no emotions about his stocks, and a great sense of timing.

what: highlight "In 1929, Kennedy's fortune was estimated to be $4 million"
said: What we do know is this. In nineteen twenty-nine, his fortune was about four million dollars. After the crash, he became a multi-millionaire by betting that prices would keep falling.

what: highlight "appointed Kennedy to be the first chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)"
said: And then, in a twist nobody could make up, President Roosevelt made Kennedy the very first chairman of the new Securities and Exchange Commission.

what: highlight "to end irresponsible market manipulations and dissemination of false information about securities"
said: Congress created it in nineteen thirty-four to end market manipulation and the spread of false information about stocks.

what: highlight "leading to a $250,000 profit"
said: Livermore was famous for these bets. The day before the great San Francisco earthquake of nineteen oh six, he had a big short bet on a railroad stock. It made him two hundred fifty thousand dollars.

what: highlight "Livermore's huge short positions made him $1 million in a single day"
said: Livermore had done it before. In the Panic of nineteen oh seven, his short bets made him one million dollars in a single day.

what: highlight "requested him to refrain from further short selling"
said: He was so effective that J. P. Morgan, the banker who had rescued the stock exchange in that panic, asked him to stop short selling.

what: highlight "using more than 100 stockbrokers to hide what he was doing"
said: In early nineteen twenty-nine, he built huge short positions again. He used more than one hundred stockbrokers so nobody could see what he was doing.

what: highlight "he netted approximately $100 million"
said: When the crash came, he made about one hundred million dollars. In today's money, that would be well over a billion.

what: highlight "In 2005, Burry started to focus on the subprime market ."
said: Now jump ahead almost eighty years. In two thousand five, a doctor turned investor named Michael Burry started studying risky home loans.

what: highlight "persuading Goldman Sachs and other investment firms to sell him credit default swaps"
said: So he paid big banks for a kind of insurance that would pay him if those mortgage bonds failed. It is called a credit default swap.

what: highlight "Burry suffered an investor revolt"
said: For a long time, nothing happened. He kept paying for the insurance, and his own investors got angry and tried to pull their money out.

what: highlight "He made a personal profit of $100 million"
said: Then the housing market broke. Burry made about one hundred million dollars himself, and more than seven hundred million for his investors.

what: highlight "In November 2025, Burry announced he was shutting down Scion Asset Management"
said: In November twenty twenty-five, Burry announced he was shutting down his fund, and started writing a newsletter instead.

what: highlight "insiders in the United States are required to file Form 4"
said: When top executives or big owners buy or sell their own company's stock, they have to report it to the government. In America, they file a form called Form Four.

what: highlight "In many countries, trading based on insider information is illegal."
said: Legal insider selling happens all the time. Trading on secret information is the illegal kind, and it can send people to prison.

what: highlight "Large stock market trends often begin and end with periods of frenzied buying (bubbles) or selling (crashes)."
said: Big market swings usually start and end with a crowd. Frenzied buying in a bubble. Frenzied selling in a crash.

what: highlight "greed in the bubbles, fear in the crashes"
said: Economists call this herd behavior. Greed pulls people in near the top. Fear pushes them out near the bottom.

what: highlight "Individual investors join the crowd of others in a rush to get in or out of the market."
said: Regular investors join the rush, buying when everyone is excited and selling when everyone is scared.

what: highlight "it remains difficult, if not impossible, to predetermine the local maximum or minimum of future prices with any precision"
said: And timing the market is extremely hard, even for experts. Nobody can reliably pick the exact top or the exact bottom.

what: highlight "using 400% margin"
said: Remember, Livermore used huge amounts of borrowed money. Back in nineteen oh one, he made one bet using four hundred percent margin. Margin means trading with borrowed money.
